title: Isometric Game
description: An ongoing project inspired by Polytopia, SimCity, and Civ VI. Built both 2D and isometric prototypes, implemented pathfinding and world saving. I plan to restart the project in C++ with better architecture and devlogs.

title: MNIST Neural Network
description: My first dive into machine learning. Wrote a neural network from scratch to classify hand-drawn digits using the MNIST dataset. Focused on understanding the fundamentals of forward propagation and backpropagation.

title: Bezier Curve Swerve Paths
description: A tool to generate smooth autonomous paths for our FIRST Robotics team's swerve drive using Bezier curves. Helped us win the Autonomous Award at the Arizona East 2023 Regional.

title: WikiFacts AI Video Project
description: An automated pipeline that generated short videos summarizing Wikipedia articles into 5 facts. Used ChatGPT, Wikipedia API, Google Images, Amazon TTS, and OpenCV to compile videos and upload to YouTube Shorts. Gained 300 subs and 150K+ views.

title: TapTech Studio
description: NFC products, from wooden necklaces with NFC tags inside to 3D-printed keychains, like a Spotify-logo keychain that opens a song when you tap it. For a Luminosity Lab event I made 300 keychains, each with its own URL that its owner could point at their LinkedIn or anything else.

title: Abstract Wave Art
description: Inspired by water caustics and wave patterns. This Python project layers and rotates mathematical waveforms (e^sin(x)) to generate intricate light-shadow maps. I used cv2 for rotation, optimized performance, and shared the generative art via an Instagram page.

title: MechVolta
description: My first Luminosity Lab project, freshman year: storing electricity mechanically in small form factors, so electric cars could rely less on rare metals. It didn’t pan out, but it taught me a lot.

title: Gravitational Physics Sim
description: A JavaFX simulation modeling orbital physics using Newton's law of gravitation and 3D vector math. I used object-oriented design and built visual representations of 3D vectors using cylinder-cone models, applying concepts from calculus and physics. It started as an honors project and led to a spot in the Photoemission and Bright Beams lab.

title: SabL-Cesium
description: A conceptual system of universal measurement units not based on Earth-centric standards like the second or meter. Built from a conversation about how units should be derived from universal constants instead of arbitrary Earth measurements.

title: ESP32 Websocket Car
description: I designed this car that hosts a website on the ESP32. The website allows you to control the car using a keyboard on any device on the same network. Modeled, printed, wired and programmed solo in C and C++, and moved the controls from HTTP requests to WebSockets to cut latency.

title: Mini CHARLOTTE
description: I designed this robot using the CHARLOTTE robot as a reference. The original CHARLOTTE was made for the NASA Big Idea Competition in 2022, and won the Systems Engineering Award. Mini CHARLOTTE is fully 3D-printed, uses a Raspberri Pi and 12 Robotis motors to control the 3 3DOF legs, and the 3 1DOF legs.

title: Toolboard
description: A dashboard that pulls all your tools into one place: email, to-do lists, Slack notifications and favourite links, as cards you can drag and resize. React + TypeScript on the front, Flask + Supabase on the back.

title: Prompter
description: An experiment in measuring prompts. It changes a prompt in small ways, like swapping words, and measures the effect on the output, to learn what makes a prompt powerful instead of guessing. Python engine, TypeScript UI, Flask backend.

title: Pantry
description: An iOS macro-tracking app, live on the App Store. Barcode scanning, receipt scanning through an LLM + Open Food Facts pipeline, RevenueCat subscriptions and a Supabase backend. Built from a web app all the way to its App Store debut.

title: Orbitscape
description: A browser-native orbit visualization platform from the Luminosity Lab, now launched as a startup with a twelve-person team. I’m building the mission-planning frontend that generates scripts for the simulation engine.

title: Particle Analyzer
description: A Luminosity Lab device that charges particles and then detects them, measuring their size and other properties. I did the CAD, which taught me to design parts for machining in metal instead of 3D printing.

title: Project Jude
description: A lifesaving submarine device at the Luminosity Lab. I did the CAD for the first version and now advise the team building the next one.

title: Zipper: Discord/Terminal AI Assistant
description: A personal assistant chatbot that can be used on Discord and in the terminal. It can answer questions, but most importantly has the ability to run bash commands on my computer. I can control my computer from my phone using it, and it can explain terminal outputs to me. Rebuilt in 2026 around Claude: each Discord thread is its own conversation, working in a folder of notes kept in git.

title: Voussoir
description: A referral-code marketplace concept, tested for demand before building: I designed the concept, bought the domain, built a waitlist and posted it to Reddit.

title: Iron Man Helmet
description: A multi-piece helmet surface-modeled in Onshape and printed on a Bambu P1S, with heat-set inserts joining the panels. A deliberate step outside my usual parametric CAD.

title: GIFs Against Humanity
description: A party game where the answers are GIFs. Everyone plays on their own phone, with an optional TV as the shared screen. No accounts or downloads: open the site, type a four-letter code, pick a nickname. Flask backend, 100 curated prompts.

title: Barrett Thesis
description: My honors thesis: designing a low-cost, open-ended STEM kit and coding curriculum for an under-resourced classroom, with a school in Kenya as the main deployment site.

title: Purchase Request Extension
description: A Chrome extension for the Luminosity Lab’s purchasing workflow: open a purchase request, click once, and the Airtable form fills itself, replacing about sixteen fields of retyping.

title: Procedural Pixel Art Trees
description: I'm bad at pixel art, so I wrote a program to make it for me. It grows a random tree branch by branch and animates it growing, then turns it into pixel art with outlines, leaves and a shadow, ready to save as an image or a video. Every tree in this forest is grown by a JavaScript port of it.

title: TileWorld
description: A top-down pygame world that generates itself in chunks as you walk: grassland and forest from my own pixel-art tiles, with menus, separate save files for each world, and tiles you can build on. The grass in this forest comes from it.

title: Stonkle
description: A stock-guessing game. You see the first three months of a random stock's chart, with the company and year hidden, and choose buy or sell. Then the next three months are revealed and you score points for being right, levelling up as you go. Flask and pandas on eight years of Yahoo Finance data.

title: Bit Tic-Tac-Toe
description: A command-line tic-tac-toe in C++ where each player's moves are stored as a 9-bit number. Checking for a win is just ANDing those bits against the eight winning patterns, so it's very fast.
